name: Zonos
description: Zyphra's open-weight zero-shot TTS engine (Zyphra/Zonos, Zonos-v0.1, trained on ~200k hours). Self-hosted only via a Gradio interface (gradio_interface.py) that binds 0.0.0.0 on port 7860 with no authentication. Shodan http.html-blind (JS-rendered SPA); identity resolves via the unauthenticated /config JSON.
auth_notes: No authentication. gradio_interface.py calls demo.launch(server_name="0.0.0.0", server_port=7860, share=share) - it binds ALL interfaces on port 7860 by default (not loopback), with no auth= argument, so an exposed host serves the UI to anyone who finds the port. share is gated by the GRADIO_SHARE env var (default False); when set it mints a public *.gradio.live tunnel. Gradio would enforce credentials only if auth= or GRADIO_USERNAME/GRADIO_PASSWORD were set - none are. No rate limiting.

shodan_dorks.rationale: Zonos serves a Gradio SPA that binds 0.0.0.0:7860 by default; the gradio-app mount div is the reliable body marker since the Zonos name is JS-rendered and not in http.html. Catches the surface for /config confirmation.
The served SPA shell embeds/references the Gradio config; combined with the canonical port this isolates Gradio surfaces to then resolve via the /config JSON that carries the Zonos app title.

Conjunctive: Gradio mount plus the inlined Zonos banner isolates it from other Gradio TTS apps - but the name resolves only when the Gradio version inlines config; otherwise fetch GET /config (unauthenticated, returns the app title) or use aimap deep-enum.
The Zonos-v0.1 model identifier in the inlined config banner or /config JSON scopes the release; the /config 'version' field also gives the Gradio version for CVE scoping.

known_vulns: Binds 0.0.0.0:7860 by default with no auth - exposed unauthenticated TTS and voice cloning out of the box on a public host
Gradio CVE-2024-1561 - arbitrary local file read via component routes on unpatched pins
Gradio CVE-2023-51449 - path traversal via /file= on Gradio 3.x < 3.47.0
Gradio CVE-2024-1727 - CSRF chain against /file and upload routes on Gradio 4.x pre-patch
SSRF via /queue/join upload proxy in the 2024 Gradio 4.x security batch
Unauthenticated GPU compute consumption - no rate limiting on inference by default
GRADIO_SHARE=1 mints a public *.gradio.live tunnel bypassing local network controls
risk_notes: Zonos is a default-exposed Gradio surface: gradio_interface.py hardcodes server_name='0.0.0.0', so unlike the loopback-defaulting cohort it serves all interfaces the moment it runs. Vectors: (1) Unauthenticated zero-shot voice cloning - attacker supplies a reference clip and synthesizes arbitrary speech in that voice (deepfake/vishing), aided by Zonos's high-fidelity 200k-hour model; (2) GPU compute theft on the ungated inference queue; (3) File-read/traversal on instances pinned to a vulnerable Gradio version (CVE-2024-1561 / CVE-2023-51449) via /file=; (4) GRADIO_SHARE tunnels publish the whole UI publicly. Shodan http.html is blind to the Zonos name (JS SPA; title 'Gradio', mount div id='gradio-app', Server 'uvicorn'); the name lives in the /config JSON, which is unauthenticated and also carries the Gradio version for CVE scoping - so confirmation is a /config fetch or JS-rendering crawl, not a body-string match. Zyphra also runs a first-party hosted playground at playground.zyphra.com/audio (out of scope for self-hosted harvesting).
deployment_notes: ~7.2k stars, not archived (last push 2025-03-05). Self-hosted only via the Gradio interface (no separate REST server in-repo); a Dockerfile and docker-compose are shipped in-repo (run the Gradio interface with --gpus=all) but no named published image is confirmed. gradio_interface.py binds 0.0.0.0:7860. Server header is 'uvicorn' (Gradio on Starlette/uvicorn). The served page is a JS SPA, so pivot on port 7860 plus the gradio-app mount, gradio_config reference, and 'Gradio' title, then read GET /config (unauthenticated) to recover the Zonos app title and the Gradio version. HuggingFace Spaces demos of Zonos are public by design.
